question_text: Show that ²⁵C₄ + Σ ⁽²⁹⁻ʳ⁾C₃ = ³⁰C₄, the sum taken over r = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

mark_split.label: Write out the five terms of the sum
Repeat the identity until one term is left

recall_prompt: Say how you would show this sum of combinations equals thirty C four — what you write out first, which identity you use, and how it collapses.
insider_note: Write all five terms of the sum first — r = 0 gives ²⁹C₃ and r = 4 gives ²⁵C₃ — then start Pascal at the 25 pair, the only pair with a C₄ partner. Two of the four marks are the written chain ²⁶C₄, ²⁷C₄, ²⁸C₄, ²⁹C₄, ³⁰C₄, ending at "= R.H.S.".

steps.label: Write out the sum
steps.margin_note: First mark. Put r = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 into ⁽²⁹⁻ʳ⁾C₃ and list the five terms; then place ²⁵C₄ next to ²⁵C₃.
steps.memory_tip: r = 0 to 4 gives FIVE terms, ²⁹C₃ down to ²⁵C₃. Put ²⁵C₄ next to ²⁵C₃.

recall.must_convey: That the sigma is expanded into its five terms ²⁹C₃ down to ²⁵C₃ and written next to ²⁵C₄.
accept: put r equal to zero to four and write twenty nine C three down to twenty five C three
expand the sigma into five terms and put twenty five C four beside twenty five C three
write out all five terms of the sum first
sigma ni expand chesi five terms rayali, twenty five C four pakkana twenty five C three
list the terms from r equals zero to r equals four

steps.why: The identity needs two terms with the same top number and lower numbers one apart. Only after the sum is written out does such a pair — ²⁵C₃ and ²⁵C₄ — appear side by side.
common_mistakes: Writing four terms instead of five — r = 0 gives ²⁹C₃ and r = 4 gives ²⁵C₃.
Leaving ²⁵C₄ at the far end instead of next to ²⁵C₃.

steps.label: Apply the identity once
steps.margin_note: Second mark. State ⁿCᵣ₋₁ + ⁿCᵣ = ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾Cᵣ and use it on the pair with top number 25: ²⁵C₃ + ²⁵C₄ = ²⁶C₄.
steps.memory_tip: ⁿCᵣ₋₁ + ⁿCᵣ = ⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾Cᵣ. Start at the smallest top number — only the 25 pair has a C₄ partner.
lines: on the pair with the smallest top number:

recall.must_convey: That the identity n C r minus one plus n C r equals n plus one C r is used on ²⁵C₃ + ²⁵C₄ to give ²⁶C₄.
accept: n C r minus one plus n C r is n plus one C r so twenty five C three plus twenty five C four is twenty six C four
use the Pascal identity on the twenty five pair to get twenty six C four
combine twenty five C three and twenty five C four into twenty six C four
twenty five C three plus twenty five C four ni identity tho twenty six C four ga rayali
the identity turns the pair of twenty fives into twenty six C four

steps.why: The identity raises the top number by one and keeps the lower number at 4, so each use produces exactly the C₄ term the next C₃ term needs.
common_mistakes: Writing the identity with equal lower numbers — they must differ by one.
Starting from ²⁹C₃; only the 25 pair has a C₄ partner at the start.

steps.label: Repeat until one term remains
steps.margin_note: Two marks. ²⁶C₄ joins ²⁶C₃ to make ²⁷C₄, and so on up to ³⁰C₄. Show every line and end with R.H.S.
steps.memory_tip: Each line raises the top by one and keeps the lower at 4. Write every line and end at '= R.H.S.'.

recall.must_convey: That the identity is applied again and again — 26, 27, 28, 29 — and the sum collapses to ³⁰C₄, which is the right-hand side.
accept: keep combining twenty six C four with twenty six C three and so on until thirty C four is left
repeat the identity four more times and it becomes thirty C four which is the right hand side
the sum collapses step by step to thirty C four
identity ni repeat cheste thirty C four vasthundi, adi R H S
twenty seven C four then twenty eight then twenty nine then thirty C four

steps.why: Each application removes one term and raises the top number by one; five C₃ terms lift ²⁵C₄ to ³⁰C₄. Ending with "= R.H.S." is what turns the working into a proof.
common_mistakes: Stopping at ²⁹C₄ — the last term ²⁹C₃ still has to be absorbed.
Changing the lower number to 3 along the way; it stays 4 at every step.
Never writing "= R.H.S." — a "show that" question ends there.
